newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: AUSTRALIA-PNG TALKS ON BOUGAINVILLE
Prime Minister John Howard and his Papua New Guinean counterpart Sir Julius Chan have held talks on the relationship between the two countries in Sydney.
In the formal and lengthy talks yesterday, Mr Howard and Sir Julius discussed the issue which has been straining bilateral relations for some time, Bougainville.
The Australian Government is strongly opposing PNG's move to hire mercenaries to assist in its military operations on the island.
The meeting came as Foreign Minister Alexander Downer again raised Australia's concerns with his PNG counterpart, Kilroy Genia.
Mr Genia later said Mr Downer was satisfied with his clarification of PNG's contract with the priavte military training company, Sandline International.
LARGE SEAS EXPECTED TO INUNDATE COASTAL QUEENSLAND
The Weather Bureau has warned that high tides combined with large seas whipped up by Tropical Cyclone Justin will inundate low-lying parts of coastal Queensland today.
The category two cyclone has remained almost stationary overnight and is about 580 km east of Cairns and 470 km northeast of Bowen.
It remains a very large system covering most of the coral sea, and is expected to gradually intensify and move slowly towards the north Queensland coast during the next couple of days.
Forecaster, Jeff Crane, says destructive wind gusts exceeding 130 kilometres an hour are likely in the Whitsundays by afternoon, spreading south to Yeppoon and north to Bowen during Monday night.
BRAVERY AWARD FOR CHOPPER CREW
A helicopter rescue crew will be recommended for a bravery award, after they risked their lives to winch a couple to safety from their floundering 15 metre yacht in cyclonic seas off Townsville.
A paramedic was lowered to the vessel and managed to pluck the Sailors aged 49 and 50 to safety -- as nearby Tropical Cyclone Justin stirred up 60 knot winds and 10 metre seas.
Australian Maritime safety Authority senior search and rescue co-ordinator, Sam Hughes, says the couple owe their lives to the three man crew from the North Queensland Rescue Helicopter Service.
PUBLIC TRANSPORT RESUMES IN MELBOURNE
Melbourne's weekend public transport strike ended at midnight, with the dispute over working conditions under privatisation deepening.
The Kennett Government has withdrawn its offer on terms and conditions, with Transport Minister Robin Cooper saying he won't negotiate further.
The Government has threatened to stand down workers and privatise The transport system in response to industrial action.
Mr Cooper says the Cabinet will consider all options when it meets on Tuesday, including going to the Industrial Relations Commission.
But Trades Hall Council secretary Leigh Hubbard says a cabinet meeting is not the way to resolve the dispute and the unions want to continue negotiating.
He says unions will decide on further industrial action after the Government clarifies its position but stand-downs would be provocative.
HOTELS LEAD PUSH FOR CLUB TAX
The Australian Hotels Association will launch a national campaign at Tweed Heads on the far north coast of New South Wales today to make Australia's Registered Clubs pay proper income tax.
National Director of the AHA Richard Mulcahy says Tweed Heads was chosen for the launch because no other area in Australia is so dominated by massive clubs.
Mr Mulcahy says despite nearly 200-million dollars in revenue over the past two years...the four largest Tweed Clubs have paid less than 10-thousand dollars in income tax between them.
He says this is less than the lowest paid employee in Tweed Heads.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
